title: Detection gaps in the pilot-controller system: analysis code for a four-decade study of ATC-related NASA ASRS incident reports (1988-2026)
description:
Reproduction code for the study Detection gaps in the pilot–controller system: a four-decade analysis of air-traffic-control-related incident reports from NASA ASRS (1988–2026), submitted to Safety Science.

The pipeline analyses 30,410 unique ATC-related reports from NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System. Hazard themes are recovered from the reporter-written narratives using BERTopic, validated convergently against the Anomaly and Primary Problem labels assigned by NASA analysts, and then linked to operational conditions, proportional trends across four decades, and—the core contribution—the detection pathways recorded in the Detector, When Detected, and Result fields.

Ten numbered scripts run in order: corpus merging and de-duplication (01), field profiling (02), descriptive tables and figures (03), BERTopic modelling (04), convergent validation (05), operational cross-tabulations (06), proportional trend estimation (07), detection-pathway analysis (08), severity proxies and the priority composite (09), and coherence, seed-stability and core-cluster sensitivity checks (10).

All random seeds are fixed at 42 and package versions are pinned, so the reported results are reproducible. The underlying ASRS reports are public US Government records and must be exported by the user from the NASA ASRS Database Online; see the repository README for the exact query and export procedure.
